Paris: Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame & Seine cruise

The 330 m Eiffel Tower was the tallest structure in the world for 41 years. At night it sparkles with 20,000 lights for five minutes every hour.

Snow on Mount Titlis · Lucerne → Interlaken

Ride the revolving Rotair cable car up Mount Titlis to play in the snow, walk through the Glacier Cave and cross the Cliff Walk. In Lucerne, see the Lion Monument and Chapel Bridge, cruise the lake for an hour and take a scenic train to Interlaken.
The Rotair was the world’s first revolving cable car, and the Titlis Cliff Walk is Europe’s highest suspension bridge, at over 3,000 m.

Rome & the Vatican in a Day

Take a high-speed train to Rome. With licensed guides, see the Vatican Museums, the Sistine Chapel and St Peter's Basilica, then go inside the Colosseum, toss a coin into the Trevi Fountain and see the Pantheon before the train to Florence.
The Colosseum held about 50,000 spectators and was voted one of the New 7 Wonders of the World in 2007. The Vatican is the smallest country on earth – our 8th country.

Florence & the Leaning Tower of Pisa

Explore Florence, the cradle of the Renaissance: the Duomo, Piazza della Signoria and Ponte Vecchio, and the postcard view from Piazzale Michelangelo. Lunch at a Tuscan villa among vineyards, then on to Pisa for the famous photo with the Leaning Tower, and a farewell dinner near Milan.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa leans about 4 degrees. It began tilting while it was still being built, more than 800 years ago.
